answer: Here is one mechanism that works: pay rewards over a slow vesting curve tied to continued correct work, because velvet only stays cheap while a farm must fund and babysit every clone for weeks before cashing anything out. Concretely, comet is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any meadow approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
